intro: An AI assistant for documentary filmmakers helps you balance intense creative editing with the heavy administrative load of production. By using voice to handle research, scheduling, and communication, you spend less time in menus and more time on your footage.
tldr: Use voice to manage your Mac without leaving your creative flow.
Get help with research, email drafting, and file organization.
Keep your focus on the timeline instead of the administrative overhead.

blocks.text: The documentary film production workflow on Mac

Your day as a filmmaker involves shifting between two very different modes. You have the deep creative work of editing and the administrative work of running a production. The edit is where the film comes to life. It requires hundreds of hours of focus. A 90 minute feature film often needs 270 hours for the base edit and sound assembly. You cannot afford to lose your flow state to a simple email or a file search.

The administrative side is just as demanding. You manage legal releases, budgets, and funding applications. You spend over half of your day on electronic communication. This takes you away from the timeline. When you are in Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, you want to stay there. Switching apps to check a calendar or find a file is a major distraction.
How an AI assistant for documentary filmmakers saves time

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It does not replace your editing software. It helps you control the environment around it. When you need to find a document, check a date, or draft a quick email, you do not need to click through folders. You hold the shortcut and ask.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur a question about what is on your screen. If you are lost in a complex app, ask how to perform a specific task. Lazur will guide you through the menus one step at a time.
blocks.title: Use voice to stay in your flow

blocks.text: Organization is the backbone of any documentary. If you lose track of your assets, you lose time. Many filmmakers use tools like Post Haste or NameChanger to keep things tidy. When you are working in Finder, you can ask Lazur to help you find specific files or remind you of your naming conventions.

items: Create a consistent folder structure for every new project.
Use Finder tags to mark footage as logged or ready for review.
Keep your raw media separate from your project files.
Use Lazur to quickly open your project root folder.

blocks.text: Communication is a massive part of your role. You are in constant contact with subjects, crew, and distributors. You spend 28 percent of your workweek in your inbox. This is time you could spend on the fine cut. Use Lazur to draft responses or find information in past threads.

Deep work is essential for a good edit. Do not let small tasks break your concentration. If you need to check a reminder or set a timer, do it by voice. Keep your hands on your mouse or your keyboard shortcuts. If you are using Premiere Pro, you likely rely on a specific set of tools. Let Lazur handle the background tasks like searching for research or drafting replies to team members.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my film for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It helps you manage your workflow by answering questions, pointing at UI elements, and drafting text.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Adobe Premiere Pro?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works on your Mac, so it can see and help you navigate any app, including Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro.

faq.question: Is my footage safe?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen and listens when you hold the shortcut. It does not store your content or use it to train AI models.
